## Enable OpenMetadata

Set `ENABLE_OPENMETADATA` to `true` in the environment that runs Mage. The next time
you start the Mage server, successful pipeline runs can publish lineage to
OpenMetadata. No block needs to be added to the pipeline.

Mage publishes lineage *after* every block in the run succeeds. A failure to reach
OpenMetadata, or a table that is missing from the catalog, is logged and reported but
never marks the pipeline run as failed.

## Configuration file

Add `omd_lineage.yaml` to the root of your Mage project. An example file is available
at `integrations/openmetadata/example_omd_lineage.yaml` in the Mage repository. To
keep the file elsewhere, set `OPENMETADATA_CONFIG_PATH` to its path.

The file has three parts:

- `openmetadata` — server URL, token, and lineage publishing options.
- `profiles` — one entry per database that the pipeline reads from or writes to. The
  `service` value is the OpenMetadata database service name.
- `pipelines` — per-pipeline switches, trigger modes, and optional block contracts.

OpenMetadata is the source of truth for the catalog. Mage only publishes lineage for
tables and columns that already exist there; it does not create database services,
tables, or columns.

## Enable lineage for a pipeline

Opt in per pipeline in `omd_lineage.yaml`:

```yaml
pipelines:
  demo_lineage:
    enabled: true
    trigger:
      modes: [on_run]
```

| Mode | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `on_run` | Publish after every successful run. |
| `on_change` | Publish after a successful run when the pipeline fingerprint changed. |
| `schedule` | Publish through the command-line interface on your own schedule. |
| `manual` | Never publish automatically; publish through the command-line interface. |

## Configuration example

```yaml
openmetadata:
  host: ${OMD_HOST:-http://localhost:8585}
  token: ${OMD_TOKEN}
  pipeline_service: mage

profiles:
  default:
    service: warehouse_demo
    driver: postgres
    database: analytics
    default_schema: public

pipelines:
  demo_lineage:
    enabled: true
    trigger:
      modes: [on_run, on_change]
```

When the pipeline finishes, Mage writes a coverage report to
`mage_data/<project_uuid>/omd_lineage/coverage.json`. It contains every published edge,
the missing catalog entities, and the number of edges left in the retry spool.

## Command-line interface

Preview the lineage plan without writing:

```bash
export OMD_HOST=http://localhost:8585
export OMD_TOKEN=...

python -m mage_ai.services.openmetadata.lineage plan \
  --project /path/to/mage/project --all
```

Publish manually (for example when a pipeline uses the `manual` trigger mode):

```bash
python -m mage_ai.services.openmetadata.lineage apply \
  --project /path/to/mage/project --pipeline demo_lineage --yes --non-interactive
```
